cpp-coding-guide — [P3] Name the new lane-selection values

The new `lane & 1` and `lane & 2` expressions encode which lane-selection bit each shuffle stage uses. The coding guide requires named `constexpr` values here, including for `1`. For example, `LANE_LOW_BIT_MASK_1` and `LANE_HIGH_BIT_MASK_2` would make those roles explicit. Apply the same rule to the new lane template arguments at lines 257–259.

The new call in `t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:302` also passes `true` directly. The guide requires a named Boolean at call sites, so use a name such as `REPEAT_TRUE` there. These are style findings, not correctness defects.

PR review: The PR body says a caller with an unlisted group size "fails to link", but at HEAD it fails to compile at the requires-clause, before any link step [should-fix].

Evidence, lines 202-204:
```
template <size_t group_heads>
  requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))
void pack_q_group_128x4(const bf16* q_group, bf16* packed) noexcept;
```
A call such as `pack_q_group_128x4<8>(...)` has no viable candidate. The compiler rejects it with "constraints not satisfied". The linker is never reached. A link failure can only happen for a size that passes group_heads_ok but has no explicit instantiation in amx_attn.cpp:333-354. The comment at amx_attn.cpp:330-332 states that the two lists are equal, so that case does not exist at HEAD either.

Reading cost: a reviewer who tests the claim by adding `<8>` sees a compile error and then doubts the rest of the bullet.

Proposed replacement for the PR-body sentence (section "How to review this PR", question 2, second bullet): "A caller with any other size fails to compile: the requires-clause on every declaration rejects it. The instantiation list and group_heads_ok must stay equal, or a size that passes the gate would fail to link instead."

PR review: The query-fill comment credits the per-head offset with catching "a pack that permutes or drops heads", but the pack in this test is a fake that copies in order, so the break the offset detects is a wrong q start pointer or stride from the dispatch [nit].

Evidence, lines 142-143:
```
// Each head carries its own offset (i / head_size), so a pack that
// permutes or drops heads cannot pass; every value is exact in bf16. The
```
The fake pack at lines 257-264 copies `input[0 .. group_heads * HEAD_SIZE_128)` into `probe.q` in order. No real packer runs here, so a permuting pack is not a break this file can see. A dropping pack is caught without the offset: a missing head leaves `probe.q[i]` at 0, and every `expected[i]` is at least 1.0. What the offset adds is a check on the pointer the dispatch hands to the packer. With the old fill (period 4), the first n_heads-1 heads of a pointer offset by one head read values identical to the expected ones. In this fixture n_kv_heads = 1 (line 82), so kv_head is 0 and the `kv_head * kv_mul * head_size` term at self_attention.hpp:1697 is always 0. The offset therefore guards a start-address or stride error, not that term. The round-2 fill at lines 180-183 has no per-head offset, so the property holds only for round 1.

Proposed replacement for the two sentences: "Each head carries its own offset (i / head_size), so the packer must read every head from its own address: a start pointer or stride that lands on the wrong head cannot pass (the fake pack copies the pointed-at values in order). Every value is exact in bf16."

alignas(64) thread_local uint16_t P[TILE_ROWS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64] = {};

body: Wade-code-review: `inline` on `store_transposed_rows` changes nothing [fwiw]. HEAD :170 reads `inline void store_transposed_rows(` under `template <int lane>` at :169, inside the anonymous namespace opened at :148 and closed at :185. The one-definition rule already lets a function template be defined in every translation unit, which is the allowance `inline` grants a plain function. The anonymous namespace gives it internal linkage anyway. So deleting `inline` changes no linkage, no type and no build. The specifier is not needed for inlining either: each instantiation `store_transposed_rows<0..3>` has a single call site (:255, :257-259) inside an internal-linkage kernel, and clang at -O3 inlines such called-once functions with or without the hint. The PR body's object compare shows it folded into `qk_rowmajor_128x4` (205 instructions, identical to main). The file's other anonymous-namespace function, `detect_and_request()` at :86, carries no `inline`, so dropping it matches the file's own idiom. No action needed.

Wade-code-review: the second round of the 16-head dispatch section repeats what the 4-head section's second round already observes [nit] (check 4, same experiment run twice). HEAD :301-302 read `exercise_page<host_bf16, amx_attn_h128g4::GROUP_HEADS_16>(page_size, /*repeat=*/true);`. Round 0 of this section is distinct: it observes `probe.pack_group_heads == 16` and its two sibling counters (:202-204) and the 16 x 128 packed values with a per-head offset (:145-148, :237). A call site that hard-coded `GROUP_HEADS_4` instead of the model's kv_mul (query heads per KV head) at self_attention.hpp:1696, :1763 or :1791 fails here and nowhere else. Round 1 observes only that a second `apply_page_range` call packs again (:177-186). The state it probes is the per-call bitset `amx_packed` (self_attention.hpp:1549), which does not depend on the group size, and the 4-head section at :292-295 already observes it. Its values at :181 carry no per-head offset, so it observes less than round 0. No break fails the 16-head round 1 and passes both the 4-head round 1 and the 16-head round 0. Cost is about 2,100 extra REQUIREs per run, well under a second, so a nit. Proposed edit: `exercise_page<host_bf16, amx_attn_h128g4::GROUP_HEADS_16>(page_size);` and drop the clause `; a second call with new queries packs again` from the section name at :299-300. The header at :17-18 needs no change. The body's Verification row `t_amx_dispatch_dtype 5,756 / 1 pass` counts assertions and must be refreshed after the change.
